classification.difficultyReason: Derives two constant-rate expressions and forms an equation comparing the remaining candle heights.

content.prompt: During a power failure, Sonia lights two identical candles of length 10 cm at 7 p.m. One candle burns out by 11 p.m. and the other candle burns out at 12 midnight. Assume that the length of each candle goes down by a constant rate.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How high is each candle at 8 p.m.?

answer.short: 11 p.m. candle: $7.5\text{ cm}$; midnight candle: $8\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The candles burn for 4 hours and 5 hours respectively, so their rates of decrease are $10\div4=2.5\text{ cm/h}$ and $10\div5=2\text{ cm/h}$. At 8 p.m., 1 hour has elapsed.

11 p.m. candle: $10-2.5\times1=7.5\text{ cm}$.

Midnight candle: $10-2\times1=8\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How high is each candle at 9 p.m.?

answer.short: 11 p.m. candle: $5\text{ cm}$; midnight candle: $6\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
At 9 p.m., 2 hours have elapsed.

11 p.m. candle: $10-2.5\times2=5\text{ cm}$.

Midnight candle: $10-2\times2=6\text{ cm}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How high is each candle $t$ hours after 7 p.m.?

answer.short: 11 p.m. candle: $(10-2.5t)\text{ cm}$ for $0\le t\le4$; midnight candle: $(10-2t)\text{ cm}$ for $0\le t\le5$. Each candle has height 0 after it burns out.
answer.worked:
Height remaining = initial height − rate of decrease × time.

11 p.m. candle: $(10-2.5t)\text{ cm}$ for $0\le t\le4$.

Midnight candle: $(10-2t)\text{ cm}$ for $0\le t\le5$.

Each candle has height 0 after it burns out.

children.label: d
children.prompt: At what time is one candle twice as high as the other candle?

answer.short:
10:20 p.m.

Set the slower-burning candle's height equal to twice the faster-burning candle's height.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the number of hours after 7 p.m. The midnight candle is taller because it burns more slowly.

$$\begin{align*}10-2t&=2(10-2.5t)\\10-2t&=20-5t\\10+3t&=20\\3t&=10\\t&=\frac{10}{3}\end{align*}$$

$\frac{10}{3}$ hours is 3 hours 20 minutes, so the time is 10:20 p.m. The heights are $\frac{10}{3}\text{ cm}$ and $\frac{5}{3}\text{ cm}$, confirming the required ratio.
